text:
maya: heads up — after the base-image roll last night autoscale gp1 nodes in us-west-2 are starting but GPU containers fail on start (after kubelet schedules).

leo: seeing it too, job pods OOM? No — they crash with library load errors. repro log from one node:
```
containerd: time="2026-07-12T03:12:14Z" level=error msg="failed to start container" error="rpc error: code = Unknown desc: failed to mount /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1: stat /host/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1: no such file or directory"
```

olga: exact error from the runtime is `failed to load libnvidia-ml.so.1: No such file or directory` — looks like libcuda / libnvidia libs aren't being bind-mounted into the container runtime.

maya: this started after we updated the base-image -> bumped nvidia-container-toolkit to 1.14 and pulled newer vendor kernel modules in the image build. New nodes come up with driver modules, but the toolkit bind behavior is flaky.

leo: quick checks:
- `nvidia-smi` on host: OK (drivers present)
- inside the runc sandbox (before container): symlinks missing under /host/usr/lib/... sometimes present, sometimes not.

sre-oncall: could be a race between nvidia-modprobe (or dkms) loading modules and the containerd create flow where the toolkit tries to resolve symlinks. If the symlink is created by post-install hook later in cloud-init, containerd wins and mounts fail.

olga: repro steps I used:
1) provision node with new image
2) `systemctl start containerd` quickly (we start it via kubelet)
3) schedule gpu pod -> fails with mount missing

olga: workaround that fixes node immediately:
```
sudo systemctl stop kubelet containerd
sudo /sbin/modprobe nvidia
sudo ldconfig
sudo systemctl start containerd kubelet
```
That makes the symlinks appear and pod starts.

maya: good catch. So root cause likely cloud-init ordering: driver install steps and postinstall scripts are finishing *after* kubelet/containerd are up. New autoscaler nodes are booting fast, kubelet starts pods immediately.

leo: mitigation path options:
- short-term: patch cluster-autoscaler/user-data to delay kubelet until `nvidia-smi` returns OK (or use systemd drop-in to make kubelet depend on a marker file).
- medium: pin nvidia-container-toolkit to previous known-good and rebuild image (rollback).
- long-term: make our machine image create the driver symlinks early (ensure modprobe + ldconfig happen in initramfs or earlier), or ensure toolkit tolerates the race.

maya: impact estimate? I scanned autoscaler pools in us-west-2 and eu-west-1: ~18 new nodes since the roll, ~12 currently cordoned by kube-probe failing. Jobs are being rescheduled to older nodes. Not a full outage but ML training fleets are impacted.

sre-oncall: immediate action: cordon the new-image node groups, prevent further scale-ups, and scale up an older image node group so workloads can move. I'll do cordon now.

deploy-bot: deploy 17579 (base-image) rolled to us-west-2 at 03:00 UTC. Rollout status: 14/20 nodes updated.

leo: I'll open a short rollback PR to pin toolkit -> 1.13 and trigger image rebuild. Also adding a kubelet systemd drop-in that adds `After=nvidia-modprobe.service` and a small readiness probe that checks `/run/nvidia-ready`.

maya: for the root cause ticket we should capture: toolkit version, kernel version, driver build, cloud-init logs ordering, and exact error messages. Olga, can you paste the cloud-init seq from one failed node?

olga: pasted snippet:
```
2026-07-12T02:59:51Z cloud-init[1234]: running postinst: nvidia-drivers 525.90
2026-07-12T03:00:05Z cloud-init[1234]: created /usr/lib/nvidia/libcuda.so.525 -> /usr/lib/nvidia/libcuda.so.1
2026-07-12T03:00:19Z systemd[1]: Started kubelet.service
2026-07-12T03:00:22Z containerd[1456]: plugin started
2026-07-12T03:00:23Z containerd[1456]: nvidia-container-toolkit: resolving /host/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 -> not found
```

leo: that ordering shows kubelet/containerd started ~14s before the symlink created. That's the race.

maya: action items:
- olga: collect cloud-init logs from 3 more failed nodes and attach to ticket (P0)
- leo: open rollback image PR + pin toolkit 1.13 and start rebuild (rollback patch + smoke tests)
- sre-oncall: cordon nodegroups and set autoscaler pause for impacted pools (in console)
- deploy-bot/infra: hold further image rollouts until we confirm fix

olga: noted, I'll attach logs in the ticket. Also adding a short shell check we can run in init to create `/run/nvidia-ready` once `nvidia-smi` OK — cheap guard for kubelet.

leo: one more note — vendor kernel modules we included changed the lib paths (`/usr/lib/nvidia` vs `/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu`), toolkit version 1.14 expects different layout. The safest rollback is the toolkit + kernel module alignment. We'll test combos in staging.

maya: thanks. please keep updates in this thread. I'll update infra-status for affected fleet and notify ML infra teams. :eyes:

sre-oncall: cordoned and paused autoscaler for group `gp1-new-image-usw2`. Scaling to old-image group now.

leo: opened PR #3482 to pin toolkit and rebuild AMI, kicking off image pipeline. I'm also adding systemd drop-in and `/run/nvidia-ready` marker as temporary mitigation.

maya: perfect. closing loop once rollback completes or we get a proper fix. :thumbsup:
